title: Ruins Stone Gate · Tianji Resonance
next_chapter_hook: The moment the stone gate opened, the third page of the Tianji Record showed signs of awakening, but was forcibly suppressed by an unknown force—that force was cold and familiar, as if coming from a forbidden place he had yet to touch.

text.content:
The faint guiding light condensed into a tiny point of light in Chen Ji's chest, like the most stubborn star in the night sky. No matter how he moved, that point of light always stubbornly pointed toward the depths of the secret realm.

The Tianji Record in his dantian grew slightly hot, a restlessness he had never experienced before, as if a beast that had slumbered for a thousand years finally caught the scent of its own kind. The patterns on the turtle shell artifact's surface began to flow slowly, faintly revealing a layer of pale golden light.

"Resonance... this is the first time." Chen Ji murmured softly, a trace of imperceptible solemnity flickering across his eyes. He had seen countless opportunities, but never had the Tianji Record so actively "called" for something.

The point of light guided him through collapsed stone pillars, around bottomless chasms, each step pressing precisely on the threads of destiny. The surrounding spiritual energy grew increasingly sparse, replaced by a desolate and ancient aura, as if this place sealed secrets from some primordial epoch.

Finally, a stone gate covered by vines and moss appeared before him.

The stone gate stood three zhang high, with an ancient seal character carved on its lintel—"天" (Heaven).

The calligraphy was bold and powerful, each stroke seeming to contain some profound principle of the Great Dao. Just one glance caused Chen Ji's Mental Sea to sting. The Tianji Record trembled violently at this moment, the pale golden light on the turtle shell artifact's surface becoming dazzlingly bright.

"Ugh—" Chen Ji groaned, forced to step back half a pace. He could clearly sense that the Tianji Record's restlessness now far exceeded any previous time—it was not warning, but... craving.

On both sides of the stone gate were inscribed lines of small text, eroded and blurred by time. Chen Ji activated his spiritual energy to examine them carefully and finally deciphered the ancient seal script:

"Heavenly Secrets must not be revealed; revelation turns the wheel of fate. Those who hold the Record should know three things—"

The second half was severed by a deep crack, the original content forever obscured.

dialogue.content:
"Three things... three things..."

An aged and ethereal voice rang out in Chen Ji's Mental Sea—the fluctuation of Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul. Chen Ji's heart lurched, and he quickly communicated through divine consciousness: "Master, do you know the secret behind this gate?"

After a moment of silence, Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out again, carrying a complex emotion Chen Ji had never heard before: "Young one, this gate... I have waited a very long time for this."

"What do you mean?"

"It means—your luck is even better than I anticipated." Mo Xiansheng's tone turned solemn. "Or rather, better than your sister anticipated."

text.content:
Chen Nian.

This name exploded in Chen Ji's Mental Sea like thunder. The fingers gripping the Tianji Record tightened slightly, knuckles whitening from the pressure. She was his missing sister, the soft spot in his grand scheme to manipulate all under heaven, the one thing his calculations could never reach.

"She knew about this gate?" Chen Ji's voice remained calm, but the churning undercurrents in his Mental Sea betrayed him.

Mo Xiansheng did not answer directly; instead, he asked an inexplicable question: "Do you see that crack?"

Chen Ji gazed again at the broken inscription on the stone gate. That crack was indeed startling, as if cleaved by some razor-sharp force.

"That is her sword mark." Mo Xiansheng's voice dropped to a low rumble. "Thirteen years ago, before she was taken, she came here."

Chen Ji shuddered.

Thirteen years ago.

That year, Chen Nian was taken by the Holy Sect under the name of "Heavenly Fate Lock Key." He was eight years old; she was merely six. It had been a rainy day when he found her in the sect's back mountain, her memories sealed by the Holy Sect's people, about to be led into the teleportation formation.

She turned her head to glance at him. Those clear eyes held no emotion, only bewilderment and fear.

That was the most helpless moment of his life.

And now, Mo Xiansheng told him—Chen Nian had been here? Had come to this gate inscribed with "Heavenly Secrets" before she was taken?

"What did she leave behind?" Chen Ji's voice was very soft, as light as a falling leaf.

choice.prompt: The ancient inscription on the stone gate was incomplete and fragmented, yet the Tianji Record's resonance grew increasingly intense. Faced with this gate that sealed Chen Nian's footprints, Chen Ji needed to make a choice—

choices.text: Forcibly Activate the Tianji Record's Resonance
choices.description: Channel one's own spiritual energy to stimulate the Tianji Record's maximum resonance, forcibly shattering the stone gate's barrier, but at the cost of consuming a large amount of Heavenly Fate Value.
choices.visible_reward: May obtain hidden information left by Chen Nian
choices.risk_hint: Unknown barriers may backlash, and the situation beyond the stone gate remains unclear

text.content:
Chen Ji took a deep breath, spiritual energy surging like a tide into his dantian. The turtle shell artifact suddenly bloomed with dazzling golden light, so bright it penetrated his robes, forming a magnificent pillar of radiance in the dark ruins.

The "天" character on the stone gate began to tremble violently, ancient barrier rune patterns shattering under the golden light's assault. A majestic force gushed from the gate's seams, confronting the Tianji Record's golden radiance in a standoff.

"Ugh—" Chen Ji felt his five脏six Fu struck by a heavy hammer, a mouthful of blood rushing to his throat. Heavenly Fate Value drained rapidly; every second felt like burning vitality.

But he did not retreat.

Because he knew—Chen Nian had been here. Before she left, she had left something on this gate.

That was her message to him. The clue he had pursued for thirteen years.

choices.text: Carefully Search Around the Stone Gate
choices.description: Do not act rashly. First use divine consciousness to carefully examine every inch of space around the stone gate, searching for other traces Chen Nian might have left.
choices.visible_reward: Discover hidden clues and avoid possible traps
choices.risk_hint: May miss the optimal timing; the stone gate's barrier has the possibility of automatic recovery

text.content:
Chen Ji suppressed the restlessness in his heart and slowly withdrew his outward spiritual energy. The Tianji Record's golden light gradually dimmed, but that resonant feeling remained, guiding him to push open this gate.

But he did not rush to act.

Thirteen years of strategic布局 had cultivated a habit in him—any seemingly easily obtainable opportunity could be a deadly trap.

He began to use divine consciousness to meticulously scan every inch of space around the stone gate, the gaps between vines, the roots of moss, the seams between stone bricks... Suddenly, his divine consciousness touched an anomaly.

In the lower right corner of the stone gate, beneath an ordinary-looking blue brick, was an extremely faint yet familiar spiritual fluctuation.

That was Chen Nian's aura.

choices.description: Place one's palm on the stone gate, requesting to open it as the Tianji Record's keeper. The gate may grant a trial or test.
choices.visible_reward: Upon successful trial, obtain the complete ancient instruction content
choices.risk_hint: Trial content unknown; may be a test specifically for the Tianji Record

text.content:
Chen Ji did not act rashly. Instead, he walked slowly to the stone door and pressed his right hand against the bold character "天" (Heaven).

In an instant, a chill surged from the stone door, racing up his arm and straight into his Mental Sea. The Tianji Record in his dantian shuddered violently, emitting a low metallic chime.

"Who enters?"

An aged yet majestic voice exploded within Chen Ji's Mental Sea. It was not Mo Xiansheng's voice, but the will contained within the stone door itself.

"Recorder of the Tianji Record, Chen Ji." Chen Ji's voice remained as calm as still water.

Another stretch of silence followed. Then the voice returned, carrying a deeper layer of meaning: "Chen... Xuan?"

Chen Ji's heart convulsed. Chen Xuan—the first master of the Tianji Record. His ancestor.

A low rumble echoed from deep within the stone door, as if a beast dormant for ten thousand years had finally opened its eyes. A faint glow began seeping from the crack, and within it, a string of blurred characters could be vaguely seen.

"Those who wield Heavenly Secrets must know three things—"

The voice was aged and authoritative, each word carrying the weight of a thousand jun.

"First: Heavenly Secrets may be revealed, but revelation shifts the wheel of fate—only one of supreme wisdom and courage can bear this burden."

"Second: Heavenly Secrets are incomplete; incompleteness breeds shackles. If shackles remain unbroken, one shall ultimately be devoured by the Heavenly Dao."

"Third—"

The voice suddenly halted. The crack blazed with blinding white light, enveloping Chen Ji entirely. He felt the Tianji Record in his dantian convulse violently, as if encountering some terrible foe.

"Third: The Tianji Record is not a tool, but a... shack...le..."

The voice cut off abruptly. The white light vanished. The stone door returned to its previous silence, only the damaged character "天" still emanating a faint, eerie glow.

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji knelt on the ground, gasping for breath. That burst of white light had nearly shredded his divine consciousness. Had the Tianji Record not shielded him at the critical moment, he would have been utterly destroyed.

"Sir..." he called laboriously within his Mental Sea, "Tianji Record is not a tool, but a shackle—what does this mean?"

Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a long time, so long that Chen Ji thought he would not answer. Finally, that aged voice spoke again, but heavier than ever before:

"Young one... some truths, known too early, become calamity."

"But I've already learned them." Chen Ji's voice was soft, yet carried undeniable resolve, "Whatever shackles they are, I will sever them. To find Nian Nian, to..."

He did not finish, but Mo Xiansheng seemed to understand.

"You and her... truly alike." Mo Xiansheng's voice carried a note of emotion, "Both so stubborn."

text.content:
Just then, the blue brick in the lower right corner of the stone door—previously discovered by Chen Ji—slid open on its own, revealing a jade slip sealed by spiritual power.

Chen Ji trembling, lifted the jade slip and wiped away the seal. A childish yet familiar voice echoed in his Mental Sea—

"Brother, if you found this place, it means you've walked the same path as me."

It was Chen Nian's voice. Six-year-old Chen Nian, who had recorded this message with her limited spiritual power before being taken away.

"I know the Tianji Record is a shackle. Every generation of recorder is slowly devoured by it, until they become puppets of Heavenly Will. Father knew, Grandfather knew, and Great-grandfather knew too... but none of them spoke of it."

"I don't want you to become like that, so I wrote it here. When you find me, we'll find a way together."

"Oh, and—I found a secret in the Holy Sect's Forbidden Grounds—the method to break the shackles is hidden within the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key' itself."

"Brother, I'm waiting for you to find me."

The voice faded, and the jade slip dissolved into scattered starlight in the air.

Chen Ji knelt before the stone door, unable to move for a long time.

Thirteen years ago, she was only six. Having her memories sealed, forcibly taken away, exploring alone in the Holy Sect's forbidden grounds... How much suffering did she endure to reach these conclusions?

And in her most desperate moments, she was still thinking—protecting her brother.

A tear fell silently, landing on the cold stone bricks.

Chen Ji raised his head. In those eyes, always calm as still water, burned a light never seen before. It was not anger, not sorrow, but something far more fierce.

"Nian Nian..." his voice was soft, yet seemed to contain the power to move mountains and fill seas, "Brother is coming to save you."

The Tianji Record in his dantian trembled lightly, as if responding to his resolve.

choice.prompt: Chen Nian's message revealed a shocking secret: the Tianji Record itself is a shackle, and the method to break it is hidden within her—the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key.' Chen Ji must decide his next move—

choices.description: Chen Nian's message mentioned the Holy Sect's Forbidden Grounds—go there now to trace her whereabouts, leaving no potential clue unexplored.
choices.visible_reward: "Might obtain more clues about Chen Nian"
choices.risk_hint: "The Holy Sect's power is vast; reckless action may lead to danger"

text.content:
Chen Ji rose abruptly, a sharp light flickering in his eyes. Thirteen years of scheming, thirteen years of patience, thirteen years of waiting—it was time to close the net.

Chen Nian is in the Holy Sect's Forbidden Grounds. If she could discover the method to break the shackles at age six, then now, at fifteen, she must have found even more.

She has been waiting for him all along.

"Holy Sect..." Chen Ji murmured, a faint smile curling his lips, "It seems this game is entering its final phase."

The Tianji Record in his dantian let out a low metallic chime, as if responding to his determination. At this moment, he was no longer the hidden, dormant waste servant, but the true Chess Player.

choices.description: Chen Nian's clues are too precious to rush. First digest the stone door's ancient teachings and the shackle information, perfect the layout, then act.
choices.visible_reward: "More thorough plan, lower risk of exposure"
choices.risk_hint: "Chen Nian's situation is unknown; delay may bring complications"

text.content:
Chen Ji drew a deep breath, forcing himself to calm down.

Chen Nian's message was certainly exciting, but the Holy Sect was no easily shaken colossus. He had spent years laying plans, each step meticulously calculated—he could not allow momentary emotional fluctuation to undo everything.

"Stone door teachings, shackle truth, Chen Nian's clues..." he mentally organized, "And the awakening signs on the third page of the Tianji Record... these pieces must be connected to see the whole picture."

He sat cross-legged before the stone door, closed his eyes, and meditative, archiving all today's gains one by one. The Tianji Record rotated slowly in his dantian, emanating a soft glow, as if helping him organize his thoughts.

"Nian Nian, wait for brother a little longer." he silently prayed, "This time, I will definitely find you."

choices.description: Mo Xiansheng seems to know more inside information. Now is the time to make him reveal the full truth—about the shackles, about Chen Nian, about the Tianji Record's true origins.
choices.risk_hint: "Mo Xiansheng may be hiding something; pressing might affect the relationship"

text.content:
"Sir." Chen Ji's voice was calm, yet carried unavoidable resolve, "You know the truth of the shackles, you know the secret Chen Nian holds as the Heavenly Fate Lock Key—what else do you know?"

Silence stretched long in the Mental Sea. Mo Xiansheng's existence was already mysterious; now his silence felt like an invisible wall, blocking Chen Ji's inquiries.

"Young one..." Mo Xiansheng finally spoke, his tone carrying a hint of helplessness, "Some things, I cannot speak. Not unwilling, but unable."

"Why?"

"Because this old one is also within these shackles." Mo Xiansheng's voice grew quieter, "You and I are both chess pieces, and the one moving the pieces... is far more terrifying than you imagine."

choices.memory_label: 墨先生似有隐瞒，态度略有保留

text.content:
Chess pieces. The one moving the pieces.

Chen Ji turned these two phrases over in his mind again and again. Mo Xiansheng's words confirmed his earlier suspicions—the Tianji Record's inheritance was not coincidence; every generation of recorder was pulled by some force toward a destined path.

But he never believed in fate.

From the moment he watched Chen Nian being taken away in the torrential rain at age eight, he swore to break every predetermined game. No matter how vast the chessboard, no matter how powerful the one who moves the pieces—he would grasp fate in his own hands.

The Tianji Record in his dantian grew faintly warm, as if sensing his determination. The patterns on the turtle shell's surface suddenly lit up, projecting a line of ancient characters into Chen Ji's vision—

"Volume One Objective Completed: Found Chen Xuan's ruins, obtained shackle warning."

"Unlocked second page knowledge: Origins of Heavenly Will."

Mo Xiansheng's voice interjected at the right moment: "Young one, you did well on this volume. Next, it's time to let you know some true secrets."

dialogue.content:
"Mr. Mo's voice echoed in Chen Ji's Mental Sea, carrying a kind of vicissitude Chen Ji had never heard before:

'The Heavenly Dao Will did not exist from the beginning. It was formed by the resentments and obsessions of countless generations of prophets—those who once held the Tianji Record, after exhausting their Heavenly Fate Values, were devoured by the Heavenly Dao. Their wills did not dissipate but merged into that massive consciousness.'

'So, the source of the Heavenly Dao Will's power... is all the previous Record Holders?' Chen Ji's voice tightened slightly.

'Precisely.' Mr. Mo's voice grew even lower, 'Including your ancestor Chen Xuan, including Chen Nian's parents—they have all become part of the Heavenly Dao Will.'

'And now, every step you take, every point of Heavenly Fate Value you consume, is providing nutrients to that consciousness.'

Chen Ji fell silent. This truth was more terrifying than he had imagined. The Tianji Record was no divine artifact but a cage—one that fattened Record Holders only to sacrifice them to the Heavenly Dao Will."

text.content:
Chen Ji slowly opened his eyes, his gaze falling on the stone door carved with the character '天' (Heaven).

The stone door remained silent, but now in Chen Ji's eyes, it was no longer just an entrance to a secret realm—it was a tombstone, recording the tragic fates of Record Holders throughout the ages.

'Chen Xuan... Ancestor.' He murmured softly, 'When you left these warnings, did you want future generations to be vigilant?'

The stone door gave no response, but Chen Ji had already found his answer in his heart.

Chen Xuan must have also rebelled once. The warning he carved into that crack was not merely an alert but hope—that someday, someone would break this cycle.

And now, that person was him.

Chen Ji stood up and bowed deeply to the stone door. This bow was gratitude and a promise.

' Ancestor above, Chen Ji is unworthy, but I pledge this broken body to shatter the chains and restore freedom to our Chen family.'

The moment he straightened up, the character '天' on the stone door suddenly burst forth with dazzling golden light.

That golden light was not an attack but a gentle yet powerful force, pouring into Chen Ji's Mental Sea through his brow center. He saw a vague figure—a man dressed in blue robes, his features seven-tenths similar to Chen Ji's, only more mature and weathered.

Chen Xuan.

The figure seemed to glance back at him, a meaningful smile at the corner of his lips, as if saying: 'Descendant, do your best.'

Then, everything returned to nothingness.

But Chen Ji clearly felt a tiny seed appear in his Mental Sea. That was the last remnant of Chen Xuan's will—what he left behind. It was not some cultivation technique or secret art but something more precious.

Hope.

A hope that refuses to give up even when trapped in dire circumstances, even when fate seems sealed.

choice.prompt: As Chen Xuan's remnant will inheritance completed, the stone door began to slowly close. At this critical moment, Chen Ji needed to make the final decision—

choices.text: Use divine sense to record the stone door's full appearance
choices.description: Record all the information on the stone door, including the traces left by Chen Nian, completely with divine sense for future use.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain complete materials for subsequent research
choices.risk_hint: The stone door is about to close, time is running short

text.content:
Chen Ji dared not delay. He immediately extended his divine sense outward, carving every detail of the stone door into the depths of his Mental Sea.

The brushwork of each stroke in the character '天', the arrangement order of the stone bricks, the growth patterns of the vines, even the lingering spiritual energy fluctuations in the air—he recorded everything meticulously.

This was a habit he had developed over many years. To scheme for the world, to leave nothing to chance, relied precisely on these seemingly trivial details.

The stone door emitted rumbling sounds, slowly closing to both sides. Chen Ji stepped back, watching as the final gap was about to disappear—

Just then, he caught sight of the last glimmer of light through the door seam.

It was an extremely small line of text, so tiny it was almost imperceptible: 'The key to the chains lies beyond fate.'

The stone door closed completely.

choices.text: Wait in front of the door
choices.description: Not in a hurry to leave, set up concealed formations in front of the stone door and observe subsequent changes here. Perhaps more secrets can be discovered.
choices.risk_hint: There may be other explorers in the ruins, easily exposed

text.content:
Chen Ji did not leave. Instead, he sat cross-legged in front of the stone door, and with a flutter of fingers, concealed formations were laid out around him.

This was what he did best—waiting.

For thirteen years, he had waited countless times in the shadows, waiting for enemies to reveal weaknesses, waiting for the right moment. This was merely another familiar wait.

The Tianji Record slowly rotated in his dantian, continuously absorbing the surrounding spiritual energy, both recovering from the earlier consumption and accumulating power for the actions ahead.

Time passed bit by bit. The ruins were deathly silent, only the occasional wind serving as a reminder that the outside world continued to turn.

Suddenly, the Tianji Record trembled again—the third page showed signs of awakening.

choices.description: Have already obtained sufficient information. Leaving now is the safest choice. There are still many matters to attend to outside—Su Qingyao, Ye Qing, Han Lie...
choices.risk_hint: There may be changes to the stone door afterward, unable to know

text.content:
Chen Ji did not hesitate. He turned and walked toward the path he came from.

He had obtained enough information—the truth of the chains, Chen Nian's clues, Chen Xuan's legacy. What remained was to connect these fragments, weaving them into a net sufficient to break the situation.

The Tianji Record grew quiet in his dantian, as if acknowledging his choice. The patterns on the turtle shell's surface gradually dimmed, but Chen Ji knew this was merely temporary peace.

The real storm was just beginning.

Passing through collapsed stone pillars, detouring around bottomless chasms, Chen Ji returned along the path he came. When he stepped out of the ruins, the sunlight made him squint slightly.

Everything outside was the same as when he entered, as if nothing had happened.

But he knew, everything was different now.

The moment Chen Ji stepped out of the ruins, the third page of the Tianji Record suddenly burst forth with blinding light.

That light was fierce and violent, like a beast imprisoned for ten thousand years finally breaking free from its chains. Chen Ji felt a sharp pain in his Mental Sea, and countless unfamiliar images flooded into his divine sense like a tide—

He saw a gigantic eye, its pupil reflecting countless stars yet radiating a suffocating coldness. That was the Eye of Heavenly Dao.

He saw a vague figure standing beneath the Eye of Heavenly Dao, surrounded by countless golden chains, each chain connected to a point of light—those were the fates of the Record Holders throughout the ages.

He also saw Chen Nian.

Fifteen-year-old Chen Nian, long hair散披, face pale, bound by countless chains on a massive altar. Her eyes were closed, yet seemed to sense something, the corners of her lips lifting slightly, revealing a bitter yet tender smile.

'Brother...'

That voice crossed through time and space, clearly falling into Chen Ji's ears.

Then, everything stopped abruptly.

Chen Ji knelt on one knee, gasping heavily. Cold sweat had already soaked through his clothes, and violent aftershocks roiled in his Mental Sea.

The signs of the third page's awakening were so intense yet so brief. He had only managed to glimpse those few images before being forcibly interrupted by some mysterious force.

That force was ice-cold yet familiar.

It was the Heavenly Dao Will.

'It is preventing me from seeing more.' Chen Ji murmured, voice hoarse yet calm, 'It does not want me to know Chen Nian's exact location... Or, it wants me to see but not approach.'

The Tianji Record in his dantian let out a low whimper, as if expressing dissatisfaction. The patterns on the third page of the turtle shell's surface flickered unsteadily, clearly in an extremely unstable state.

Chen Ji took a deep breath and slowly stood up.

He knew the Heavenly Dao Will had already noticed him. Every step from now on would be more dangerous.

But he had no choice.

For Chen Nian, to break the chains, to no longer be a puppet of the Heavenly Dao Will—he had to continue.

Even if the abyss yawned before him, even if his opponent was the lofty Heaven itself.

Sunlight fell upon Chen Ji, stretching his shadow long.

He raised his head, gazing toward the distant horizon. There, clouds rolled and surged, seemingly calm yet secretly turbulent.

The friction among the three great sects continued, the demonic path's invasion had already shown signs, and the opening of the Ancient Forbidden Land attracted countless forces stirring with ambition. And he, Chen Ji, this surface-leveltrash servant, stood at the center of every storm.

The Tianji Record grew quiet in his dantian, like a beast that had fed and was satisfied. But Chen Ji knew this was merely temporary peace.

The truth of the chains had been revealed.

Chen Nian's trail had surfaced.

Chen Xuan's legacy had been passed into his hands.

Now, it depended on how he played his pieces.

'The chess game is set, victory or defeat undetermined.' Chen Ji murmured, a slight smile at the corner of his lips, 'Everyone—'

He turned and walked toward the direction of Tianqing Sect.

'The show has just begun.'

The moment the stone gate opened, the third page of the Tianji Record showed signs of awakening, yet it was forcibly suppressed by an unknown force—that force was cold and familiar, as if coming from a forbidden land he had yet to touch.

Chen Ji clutched his chest, feeling the lingering sting in his Mental Sea. The third page of the Tianji Record had clearly awakened halfway, yet it was forcibly pressed down by that enormous eye—the Heavenly Dao's Eye.

What was it afraid of?

Or rather—what was it afraid of him seeing?

Chen Ji slowly clenched his fist, his knuckles turning slightly white from the force. He raised his head toward the horizon, and behind those clouds, as if there were a pair of invisible eyes watching him, cold and indifferent.

「Watching me?」 he murmured softly, his voice carrying a hint of mockery, 「Then watch carefully.」

「Watch how I... sever every chain you've laid upon me.」
